summary: Selected Pro Proposal 1 from the two cross-review survivors and implemented an exact two-copy composition audit of the Generation-31 Walsh Gram. Exact one-copy DP gives d_1^2=216, and residual-branch accounting gives matched two-copy control minimum 288. Despite 125 emitted cross-copy moment rows, compatible G11/G13 parity witnesses have zero residual and cost 432=2d_1^2, so strict superadditivity fails. This is a finite counterexample to this coupling rule only.
hypothesis: Global degree-at-most-three moment rows spanning two overlapping copies might make one-copy parity witnesses incompatible and force d_2^2>2d_1^2 while preserving control minimum 288.

tests.finding: Verified exact one-copy minimum 216, exact two-copy control minimum 288, 125 cross-copy moment rows, coefficient interval [-4,5] through 432, and a zero-residual two-parity witness of cost 432=2d_1^2.
The verifier compiles and the emitted rank-144 obstruction/control manifest is valid JSON.
The Generation-31 source Gram still verifies after reuse in the composition audit.

next_experiment: If composition is continued, freeze the surviving noncommuting signed-permutation edge rule before search and require an exact evaluation of the same compatible two-parity witness; kill immediately if its edge energy is boundary-additive or if the two-copy obstruction cost remains at most twice the exact one-copy cost.
